newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Qantas cool on "no frills" operation.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Qantas cool on "no frills" operation.

text.p: Qantas Airways Ltd managing director James Strong said on Thursday the airline had no intention of creating a stand alone "no frills" airline to compete with Air New Zealand Ltd's Freedom Air on the trans-Tasman route.
Strong told a news conference such operations were not sustainable long run, although he said he could not comment on whether Freedom Air would continue in the long run.
"We review all sorts of options, but I can tell you we have no intention of suddenly setting up some sort of equivalent to Freedom Air," Strong said.
Earlier, Qantas announced a 2.1 percent rise in net profit for the six months to December 31 of A$151.4 million.
Qantas said pre-tax and interest earnings from its international operations rose to A$168.3 million in the half year from A$163.3 million in the previous comparable half.
But Qantas said intense price cutting on the Australia-New Zealand route restrained growth in international earnings.

Freedom Air, a subsidiary of Air New Zealand unit Mount Cook Airlines, was set up in late 1995 to take on the booming private budget airline, Kiwi International Airlines Ltd, which was based in the North Island provincial city of Hamilton.
First Kiwi and then Freedom slashed prices on some Trans-Tasman routes almost in half over 1995 and 1996.
But the competition was so hot it drove Kiwi into voluntary liquidation under a mountain of debts in September 1996.
"There has been a period of heavy discounting and it turned out the party initiating that was operating sub-economically with the invevitable result," Strong said.

"I don't know how many times this has to happen, but every time it starts everyone says 'hallelujah isn't this wonderful' and then when a sub-economic operation bankrupts, everyone is very disappointed and surprised," he said.
"It really isn't a very good way to run any business to charge prices which are below your costs of operation. It's not a very sound long-term strategy," he said.
Strong however saw continued aggressive price competition on the Australia-New Zealand route.
Air New Zealand has said it wanted to keep operating Freedom, despite Kiwi's exit from the market.
